check: Names say what a value is or what a function does; no `data`, `temp`, or `x` for domain values.
why: Vague names force readers to trace every line to understand what a value represents.

check: Each function does one job; a function that validates, transforms, and formats is split into focused helpers.
why: Mixing validation, business logic, and formatting in one function makes each part harder to test and reuse.

check: Arguments and caller-owned objects or arrays are not mutated unless the spec explicitly requires in-place mutation.
why: Mutating caller inputs causes silent side effects and stale-state bugs elsewhere in the program.

check: Errors are thrown or returned explicitly on invalid input or failure; nothing is swallowed by an empty `catch`.
why: Swallowing errors or returning silent fallbacks hides root causes and corrupts downstream state.

check: Unexplained numeric or string literals that carry domain meaning are extracted into named constants.
why: Magic literals obscure business rules and cause drift when the same value must be updated in multiple places.

check: No commented-out code, unreachable branches, unused variables, or leftover `console.log` calls.
why: Dead code clutters the module and misleads readers about which paths are actually executed.

check: No needless cleverness such as nested ternaries or `reduce` where a direct loop or method is clearer.
why: Over-compressed expressions slow down reading and hide off-by-one or precedence bugs.
